outer.color_note: Two bodies on one baseplate: a vertical aluminum cooling-tower cylinder inside a sheet-metal rear case, joined by a semi-rigid bellows to a lift-off sample-chamber housing with 5 round windows and a flat top lid. Manual: 'the vertical aluminum cylinder inside the sheet-metal rear case'. Beam height 137.1 mm from table (QD datasheet). Mass 29 kg. Window retaining rings are Delrin. Separate off-table units: water-cooled compressor 46 x 45 x 57 cm 73 kg, 4U system control unit, 6U vacuum control unit.

sample_space.description: Sample-in-vacuum: 53 mm diameter x 63 mm high volume inside the bolt-on radiation shield, enclosed by the lift-off outer vacuum housing. Access by lifting the top lid/window assembly and then the radiation shield cap. Montana's own US brochure lists the sample space as Ø53 mm x 116 mm (likely measured to the top window rather than inside the shield).

notes: Standard configuration (no magneto-optic, no 1.2 K OneK-Optic, no nanopositioner). Sample-space height conflict: QD Europe datasheet says 53 x 63 mm inside the radiation shield; Montana's US brochure says Ø53mm x 116mm - the catalog uses 63 mm. Stage temperatures 27-28 K / 2.4-2.7 K are the manual's 'example' base-temperature table for a standard CryoAdvance-50, with the platform spec of <3.2 K; the sample lags Stage 1 by ~100 K during cooldown. Working distance: horizontal >25.3 mm, vertical >8.8 mm; acceptance angle 60 deg full. Heat load if a cold window is removed: 50-100 mW per window. Cooling power 130 mW at 4.2 K; cooldown ~2 h; vibration <5 nm p-p. GM cryocooler is suspended in the cooling tower with a vibration-damping support and a semi-rigid bellows to the sample chamber; whole assembly bolts to the optical table at 45 or 90 deg.
